# ECN-2026-031 Change notice - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P2, line P2-L2
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

Reason for change
- Background: During routine operation and post-implementation review of the previous control update (see ECN-2026-028) operators and maintenance noted inconsistent quench initiation timing on EQ-P2-L2-HT02. Analysis of event logs and furnace control sequences found variable delay between the quench command and actual quench start that could exceed acceptable process variability limits for ring rolling heat treat cycles.
- Purpose: The change standardizes the maximum allowable delay between quench command and quench initiation for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 to ensure repeatable metallurgical outcomes and reduce rework. The updated maximum quench delay value is set to 16 seconds. This is a process control limit required to maintain hardness and microstructure results within the established acceptance criteria referenced in QS-PROC-08.
- Rationale: Consistent quench timing is critical for ring rolling forgings to achieve target mechanical properties. The furnace control hardware and the quench system response have adequate capability to meet a stricter maximum delay; formalizing the limit and updating procedures eliminates ambiguity in operator response and maintenance diagnosis.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02 control logic and operator guidance are affected. Physical hardware requiring inspection is the quench actuation circuit and associated interlocks as identified in MM-P2-L2-HT02.
- Documents: Update MM-P2-L2-HT02 maintenance checklist and procedures to include verification steps for the new quench delay limit and record-keeping requirements. Update operator work instructions under the P2 line to include the 16 seconds quench delay maximum and related monitoring actions. Ensure QS-PROC-08 references the revised operational control verification for EQ-P2-L2-HT02.
- Training: Operators and maintenance personnel assigned to P2-L2 must be notified and trained on the change. Training shall cover the impact of quench delay on product quality, how to monitor and record quench timing, and escalation steps if the limit is exceeded.

Implementation
- Control change: Modify EQ-P2-L2-HT02 PLC sequence to implement a hard alarm when measured delay from command to quench initiation exceeds 16 seconds. The sequence change will also log the measured delay value in the furnace event log for each heat treat cycle.
- Operator procedure updates: Revise the furnace start-up and cycle monitoring checklist to require the operator to verify quench initiation within the 16 seconds maximum after the quench command is issued. If the alarm occurs, the operator will follow the escalation steps defined in MM-P2-L2-HT02 and notify maintenance per plant communication protocol.
- Maintenance actions: Add an item to MM-P2-L2-HT02 requiring verification of quench actuator response time during scheduled maintenance and after any control changes or actuator repairs. Maintenance records must include the measured response verification outcome and any corrective actions taken.
- Example scenarios:
  - Normal cycle: Operator issues quench command; PLC measures delay and logs value; no alarm if value is within 16 seconds; record entry appended to the cycle log.
  - Alarmed cycle: PLC measures delay greater than 16 seconds; system generates alarm, logs the delay value and timestamp, and inhibits loading of subsequent work until maintenance review is completed per MM-P2-L2-HT02. Operations will quarantine affected parts per QS-PROC-08 until disposition.
- Records to keep:
  - Furnace cycle log entries containing measured quench delay and outcome for each cycle.
  - Maintenance verification records from MM-P2-L2-HT02 showing quench actuator response checks and corrective actions.
  - Training attendance and competency acknowledgment for operators and maintenance staff covering the new 16 seconds maximum quench delay requirement.
  - Nonconformance records and dispositions processed under QS-PROC-08 for any parts impacted by quench delay exceedance.
- Timing and coordination: Implementation will be coordinated between process engineering, controls, operations, and maintenance to minimize production disruption. Changes to PLC code and MM-P2-L2-HT02 documentation shall be version controlled and tested in a controlled environment before deployment to EQ-P2-L2-HT02.

Approvals
- Required approvals: Process Engineering, Controls Engineering, Maintenance Management, Quality Assurance, and Operations Management must review and sign off on the change prior to deployment.
- Quality review: QA will confirm the change documents cross-reference QS-PROC-08 and that the 16 seconds maximum quench delay is reflected in inspection and disposition workflows.
- Post-implementation review: After deployment, a follow-up review will examine furnace cycle logs and maintenance verification records for at least one production run to confirm compliance with the 16 seconds limit and evaluate any residual process variability. Findings will be documented and, if necessary, addressed via subsequent ECN referencing ECN-2026-028.
- Related documents: This change implements and references maintenance and procedure updates in MM-P2-L2-HT02, follows the corrective thread begun under ECN-2026-028, and aligns with quality handling per QS-PROC-08.

Distribution list and records retention
- Distribution: Process Engineering, Controls, Maintenance, Operations P2-L2, Quality Assurance.
- Retention: All records related to this change including PLC change logs, furnace cycle delay logs, maintenance verification, and QA dispositions will be retained per plant records practice and made available to Quality and external auditors upon request.

End of notice.
